level.title: Elementary: city, travel, routines, health
goals: Find your way around a Brazilian city
Talk about past trips with pretérito perfeito
Describe routines, health, and future plans

lessons.title: Around the city (estou no/na)
lessons.learn: Location uses ESTAR: ESTOU EM CASA (I am at home). EM melts: EM+O=NO, EM+A=NA: ESTOU NO BANCO (at the bank), NA PRAÇA (at the square). Esquerda (left), direita (right), em frente (ahead)!

grammar.title: ESTAR + em/no/na
grammar.explain: ESTOU = I am, ESTÁ = you/he/she is. EM + O = NO (no banco), EM + A = NA (na praça). ESTOU NO HOTEL = I am at the hotel.
mistakes: Saying SOU em casa — location is always ESTAR.
Saying EM O banco — melt it: NO banco.

dialogue.en: Excuse me, where is the station?
It is over there, on the right.
No, it is near. Five minutes.

lessons.title: Travel and pretérito (simple past)
lessons.learn: Finished trips use PRETÉRITO PERFEITO: VIAJEI (I travelled), VIAJOU (you/he/she travelled). -AR verbs: -EI (eu), -OU (você/ele/ela). FALEI, COMPROU, CHEGOU!

grammar.title: Past -AR: viajei, viajou
grammar.explain: Drop -AR, add -EI (I), -OU (você/ele/ela). VIAJEI = I travelled. COMPROU = you/he/she bought. ONTEM (yesterday) loves this past!
mistakes: Saying VIAJO for the past — past I = VIAJEI.
Forgetting ONTEM goes with finished past, not present.

dialogue.t: Sim, viajei para o México. Visitei a praia.
dialogue.r: seeng, vee-ah-ZHAY pah-rah oo MEH-shee-koo. vee-zee-TAY ah PRAH-yah.
dialogue.en: Yes, I travelled to Mexico. I visited the beach.

lessons.title: Daily routines (reflexive verbs)
lessons.learn: Routines bounce back: ME LEVANTO = I get (myself) up. ME = myself, SE = yourself/himself/herself (você!). Mornings run on ME/SE: levantar-se, banhar-se, vestir-se!

grammar.title: Reflexive ME/SE: me levanto
grammar.explain: LEVANTAR-SE = to get up. ME LEVANTO (I get up), SE LEVANTA (você/he/she gets up). The little word points back — don't drop it!

examples.en: Do you bathe in the morning?

mistakes: Saying LEVANTO without ME — it means 'I lift', not 'I get up'!
Saying TE (Portugal) in Brazil — Brazil uses SE for você.

dialogue.t: A que horas você se levanta?
dialogue.r: ah kee OH-rahsh voh-SEH see leh-VAHN-tah?
dialogue.en: What time do you get up?

dialogue.t: Me levanto às sete e tomo banho.
dialogue.r: mee leh-VAHN-too ahsh SEH-chee ee TOH-moo BAH-nyoo.
dialogue.en: I get up at seven and shower.

lessons.title: Health and future (vou + verb)
lessons.learn: At the doctor: MINHA CABEÇA DÓI = my head hurts. Future with IR: VOU VIAJAR = I am going to travel. VOU, VAI + verb. The plan verb never changes!

grammar.title: Future: vou/vai + verb
grammar.explain: VOU = I go, VAI = you/he/she goes. VOU + verb = I am going to…: VOU COMER = I am going to eat. The second verb never changes!
mistakes: Changing the second verb: VOU VIAJAR, never VOU VIAJO.
Saying EU VAI — I go is VOU.

dialogue.en: No, but I am going to rest.

lessons.title: Clothes and shopping (este/esse)
lessons.learn: Shop in Portuguese! A CAMISA, OS SAPATOS. Point with ESTE (this, near me) and ESSE (that, near you): ESTA CAMISA (this shirt), ESSE VESTIDO (that dress).

grammar.title: ESTE vs ESSE: this vs that
grammar.explain: ESTE/ESTA = this (near me). ESSE/ESSA = that (near you). They match gender: ESTA camisa, ESSE vestido, ESSA loja. (AQUELE = far from both!)
grammar.pattern: este/esta + near thing · esse/essa + your thing
mistakes: Saying ESTE camisa — camisa is feminine: ESTA camisa.
Using ESSE for things in your hand — near you is ESTE.

lessons.title: Weather scenes (fazia, havia)
lessons.learn: Weather stories use IMPERFEITO: FAZIA SOL (it was sunny), HAVIA VENTO (there was wind). Just two phrases paint any past sky!

grammar.title: First imperfeito: fazia, havia
grammar.explain: FAZIA SOL/FRIO/CALOR = it was sunny/cold/hot. HAVIA + noun = there was…: HAVIA SOL (there was sun). Weather past = imperfeito, always!
mistakes: Saying FEZ SOL for scenes — weather stories use FAZIA.
Saying HÁ for past — past needs HAVIA.
